title: Acceptance rate-limit diagnosis and idle observer fix
diagnosis: The old browser observed pending and cancelled phase-zero offers every 250 ms.
Two such observers reproduced HTTP 429. A shared transport cooldown then also rejected acceptance attempts.
The previous generic error remained visible after the offer expired, suggesting synchronization was still in progress.

networkBefore.pattern: Two reads every 250 ms, stop at first rate limit
networkBefore.response: Too many requests from this caller. Try again later.

changes: Pending invitations use a two-second observer; lobby status changes trigger an immediate fresh read.
Confirmed terminal or cancelled empty matches stop polling. Unknown, pending or active engine state remains observable.
Rate-limited acceptance shows a countdown. Retry is disabled until Retry-After elapses.
Acceptance errors belong to their offer and disappear on cancellation or rotation.
Accepted transactions are reconciled from receipts and never automatically resent.

checks: Offline coordinator does not freeze a healthy direct engine lane
Final-tick revert plus 429 recovers the result without reconnecting
Unknown submission stops writes but preserves result transition
Room rotates to a new invitation before the previous result is recovered
Next match refreshes an uncertain SDK nonce without a passkey ceremony
The current tab can restore its session; a second controlling tab is still rejected
Exact per-match ELO displayed after fresh read
Actual receipt confirms the matching player
Two consensual acceptances start a friendly match

limitations: The provider still enforces a quota. These samples do not establish its complete window or scope.
This patch reduces idle traffic; sustained multi-arena gameplay capacity is not established by these tests.
The live friendly test used disposable unfunded SDK identities, not a physical Mera authenticator.
Existing tabs need a reload to stop their old polling loops.
